sections.h2: What should a Newnan, GA homeowner know before selling?
sections.html:
Newnan is the Coweta County seat, roughly 35 miles southwest of Atlanta on Interstate 85, and it spreads across about 19.5 square miles. Owners here tend to weigh a listing against a private sale or an as-is cash purchase, and the answer usually follows the age of the house and how fast you need to be done.

Census Bureau figures show 45,867 people in Newnan in mid-2025, 8.0 percent more than the 42,451 in the 2020 base. The 2020 to 2024 survey counts 17,180 households. In it, 58.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, the typical owner-occupied home is valued at $364,700 and median rent is $1,542. A bungalow near the square and a subdivision house out by the bypass will not match those averages, so look at what sold nearest to you.

sections.h2: Why do Newnan's older houses draw buyers?
sections.html:
Newnan was incorporated in 1828 on a grid with a nine-block downtown around the courthouse, and its streets honor Jackson, Jefferson, Washington and Madison. Cotton money and the passenger railroad, which opened in 1851, pushed it into the ranks of the richest towns per person in America by the mid 1800s. The R.D. Cole company started as a sawmill in 1854 and built most of the city's homes from the 1880s into the early 1900s, which explains the shared woodwork details. The Battle of Brown's Mill in July 1864 happened three miles south, and the town escaped much of the war's destruction, which is why antebellum houses survive. Its nickname is the "City of Homes."

The city's historic district page lists seven districts, and several are residential:

  • Cole Town grew around the Cole company and carries its woodwork.
  • College-Temple, laid out in 1828, has tree-lined streets, churches and a former academy lot.
  • Greenville-LaGrange covers 61 acres along two highways, with the oldest and grandest houses on the main streets.
  • Platinum Point is a 43-acre district of early 20th century houses north of town.
  • Newnan Cotton Mill and Mill Village includes a mill now converted to loft apartments.
  • Chalk Level, about 261 acres in southeast Newnan, joined the Georgia Register of Historic Places on October 24, 2025 and the National Register on January 29, 2026.

If your house is in one of them and exterior changes are planned, ask Planning and Zoning at 770-254-2354 whether design review applies.

sections.h2: What permits and local rules affect a Newnan sale?
sections.html:
The Building Department sits upstairs in City Hall at 25 LaGrange Street and takes permit applications on weekdays until 4:30 p.m. An application must include:

  • A site plan and a building plan
  • A ResChek or Comchek compliance report
  • Contractor licenses and a subcontractor list
  • The applicable fees

Records of past work help here, because unrecorded additions tend to show up under a buyer's inspection.

Tree work is another local rule. A homeowner pays no fee to remove trees on a single-family lot until more than five come down at once in a calendar year, while anyone paid to cut trees needs a permit for each one eight inches across or larger. Specimen trees follow separate rules.

Drive times matter for showings. The city sends northbound travelers off I-85 at Exit 47 and west three miles on Highway 34, and southbound travelers off at Exit 41 and north 3.5 miles on Highway 29. Coweta's sales tax is 7 percent, and local SPLOST money has paid for projects such as the Poplar Road interchange, the Newnan Bypass, the Greison Trail roundabout, the Linc and the historic courthouse.

sections.h2: Which Coweta senior school tax exemptions can a buyer claim?
sections.html:
Coweta grants a basic homestead exemption to owners who live in the home on January 1, and its local senior school tax tiers carry no income limit. The county lists these 2026 amounts:

Coweta senior school tax exemptions, 2026
CodeAge by January 1School tax exemption
LC65$75,000
LE71$100,000
LG75Full exemption

Source: Coweta County Exemptions page, which adds that the tiers can combine with veterans exemptions through a separate application.

A homestead exemption stays with the person, so the buyer files a new application with the Assessors' Office. The county allows each individual or married couple just one.

sections.h2: How do Coweta assessments and tax bills work in Newnan?
sections.html:
The Assessors' Office at 37 Perry Street sets values, and the Tax Commissioner at 87 Newnan Station Drive bills and collects. The 2026 notices went out on June 19, and the 45-day appeal window closed August 3, 2026. Later years carry later dates, and each notice states its own.

October brings the bills. One goes to the legal owner as of January 1 and another to the current owner on the Assessors' file, so a house sold after New Year's produces two. A parcel with an unresolved appeal gets a temporary bill set at 85 percent of the proposed value, and the final ruling produces a refund or an additional charge. Residential homestead bills for 2026 also carry the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant credit.

Homeowners with escrow should forward the bill to their servicer, because the county says lenders often pay just weeks ahead of the deadline. Card payments add 2.5 percent (3 percent for American Express), and an online e-check costs $1.50. Call the Assessors at 770-254-2680 or the Tax Commissioner at 770-254-2670.

sections.h2: How do I clear out a Newnan house before listing it?
sections.html:
The city's FAQ makes cleanout simple. Junk pickup needs no appointment: set items by the street on your regular collection day. Yard debris and bulk waste go through the Sanitation Department at 770-253-0327. Bagged trash must sit inside the cart, and the city will not take anything left beside it, although a second cart can be added. Newnan's AMWASTE service puts trash and recycling in one container.

Burning is allowed only with a permit from the Fire Marshal, reachable at 770-253-1851, extension 302. If a basement or outbuilding is full, start the cleanout early so inspectors and buyers can see the structure.

The Superior Court Clerk's Real Estate Division keeps every Coweta record and files documents daily in arrival order. The posted fees include $25 for a deed, $10 for a plat and $1 a page for copies. Personal checks are refused. The PT-61 transfer tax form must be e-filed with every title change, and self-filers need identity verification, while attorneys, lenders, title companies and licensed brokers may file on paper.

Georgia's $1-per-first-$1,000 transfer tax, with 10 cents per further $100, shows on the settlement statement too. Owners can also sign up for free real estate fraud alerts through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority.

sections.h2: When does a cash buyer make sense in Newnan?
sections.html: A cash purchase fits a house with deferred repairs, an inherited property or a hard deadline, and a listing fits a house in good shape with time to spare. Compare offers on price, closing date and recording costs, and name any liens, tenants or estate issues up front.

faqs.q: Do I owe Coweta property tax after selling mid-year?
faqs.a: Possibly, because Coweta bills the January 1 owner of record and also mails a bill to the newest owner. Put the payment duty in the contract and settle it at closing.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 Newnan appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Coweta's 2026 window ran 45 days from the June 19 notice date and closed August 3. A future notice prints its own deadline. Call 770-254-2680 for help reading it.

faqs.q: Do Newnan's historic districts limit repairs?
faqs.a: They may. The city lists seven districts, including Cole Town, College-Temple, Downtown and Chalk Level. Call Planning and Zoning at 770-254-2354 before exterior work.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Coweta County?
faqs.a: The clerk lists $25 for a deed. Georgia's separate transfer tax is $1 for the first $1,000 of price plus 10 cents for each added $100 or fraction.

faqs.q: Who files the deed after a Newnan closing?
faqs.a: Typically the closing attorney or title company. Self-filers must e-file after identity verification.
